name: Polymalformative Genetic Syndrome with Increased Risk of Developing Cancer
aliases: Congenital Multisystem Malformation Syndrome with Cancer Predisposition
Genetic Multimalformation Syndrome with Oncogenic Risk

criteria.description: Presence of multiple congenital malformations affecting at least two organ systems
Documented increased risk or occurrence of malignancies in patient or first-degree relatives
Identification of pathogenic variant in known associated gene(s) by molecular genetic testing
Supportive clinical features such as developmental delay, growth retardation, or dysmorphic facial features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple congenital malformations affecting at least two organ systems, documented cancer predisposition, and genetic confirmation of pathogenic variant
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical genetics and oncology assessment.

pathognomonic.notes: Involving skeletal, cardiac, and renal anomalies
Including leukemias and solid tumors in childhood

common.notes: Characteristic facial gestalt varies by syndrome subtype

occasional.notes: Including septal defects and valve anomalies
Such as horseshoe kidney or hypoplasia
May be related to hematological malignancies

rare.notes: Occasional epilepsy associated with brain malformations

laboratory: Cytopenias or abnormal blood counts indicating hematologic malignancy
Elevated tumor markers depending on cancer type
imaging: Congenital malformations detected by ultrasound, MRI, or CT
Tumor masses identified on imaging studies
genetic: Pathogenic variants in tumor suppressor genes or developmental genes identified by sequencing
Chromosomal abnormalities or copy number variations detected by microarray
other: Family history of similar malformations and cancers

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly cancer predisposition without multiple congenital malformations
Bone marrow failure with congenital anomalies
Distinct facial features and cardiac defects without increased cancer risk

redFlags: Multiple congenital anomalies involving multiple organ systems
Early onset or family history of diverse malignancies
Unexplained cytopenias or abnormal blood counts in a child with malformations
references: Orphanet: Polymalformative Genetic Syndrome with Increased Risk of Developing Cancer, ORPHA:183422
